newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary shares end mixed, TVK, Pick hit record highs.
newsitem.headline: Hungary shares end mixed, TVK, Pick hit record highs.

text.p: Hungarian shares closed mixed on Thursday as the market was seeking factors to trade on, dealers said.
The BUX index closed at 3,674.61 points, down 2.32.
Chemicals maker TVK extended its gains to a record high in brisk trade.
"TVK went up but it could not pull up the whole market," said Istvan Simon of Concorde Securities.
He added that the market reversed the rising trend of the past week as it lacked incentives for large price movements,
No corporate news was published recently, the U.S. market was closed on Thursday, and the Dow index was not seen rising much in the next few days, he added.

Dealers said TVK's price had been depressed by expectations that the market may be flooded by the planned sale of a 10.5 percent stake by Tiszaujvaros municipality. However, it rose once the stake was sold outside the bourse last week.
"Some companies sought TVK very strongly," said New York Broker's Kalman Schuszter. "This was the cheapest stock on the bourse.
TVK rose to a record high of 1,535 forints and ended at 1,530, up 100, but dealers said the stock was still undervalued.
The oil and gas company MOL reversed a rising trend which followed the annnouncement of energy prices for 1997 one week ago, falling 40 forints to end at 1,825.
"This was simple correction, there was no demand," a dealer said.
Kalman Schuszter said MOL's turnaround was a warning sign for the market, which was likely to stagnate or ease in the next few days.
BUX index futures rose by 10 to 21 points, but the December 1996 maturity, which closed at 3,709.5, was still barely above the spot BUX index, Schuszter added.
